Petitioners have filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ for the death of Krishnappa M., in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
That on 12.03.2022 at about 5.30 p.m., Krishnamma M., was proceeding by riding the TVS XL vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA 43H7152 from his Agricultural land slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules.

While he reached Dandiganahalli Vijayapura road, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru District, suddenly the rider of Bajaj Pulsar vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA43 W4809 came on the said road in a rash or negligent manner, without following the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the aforesaid TVS XL vehicle in which Krishnappa was proceeding.
As a result, Krishnappa M., was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately deceased Krishnappa M., was shifted to Akash Hospital, Devanahalli in an 108 Ambulance, even after better treatment deceased succumbed to injuries.
Thereafter, postmortem was conducted at Community Health Center, Vijayapura, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru.
The petitioners have shifted the dead body to their residence by hiring the vehicle and performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies by spending more than Rs.1,00,000/.
1St petitioner
being the wife of deceased has lost her husband and petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 being the daughter and son have lost love and affection of their father.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners were undergoing deep mental shock.

sentences.text: Due to death of deceased, the petitioners are facing difficulty and financial hardship.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash or negligent riding of Bajaj Pulsar vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA43W 4809 by its rider.
The Vijayapura Police have registered the case against the rider of aforesaid vehicle in Cr.No.24/2022 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 338 and 304A of IPC.
The 1 st respondent is the RC owner of aforesaid vehicle and the 2 nd respondent is the insurer and insurance policy was valid at the time of accident.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
With these averments petitioners prays to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st respondent remained absent, hence he was placed Exparte.
The 2nd respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

4. The 2nd respondent/Insurance company admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its validity with respect to Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA43W4809 and contended that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, valid and effective driving licence held by the rider of offending vehicle, valid R.C.
Further, contended that, the 1st respondent has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134 (c), 158(6) of M.V. Act.
The 2nd respondent has contended that, the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA43W4809 was not at all involved in the accident.
Further contended that, after through investigation the police have filed charge sheet against the deceased by stating that, the deceased himself was solely responsible for the alleged accident.

The petitioners have suppressed the material facts and cooked up false story and filed complaint after lapse of one day of the alleged accident by colluding with the police and owner of offending vehicle only to get compensation from this respondent.
It is the contention of 2nd respondent that, the deceased was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
The rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA43W4809 was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and it is clear violation of policy conditions.

The 2nd respondent has denied the age,
occupation and income of deceased, dependency of the petitioners on the deceased.
The claim made by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With these averments, the 2nd respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1.Whether petitioners prove that, Krishnappa N., had met with an accident on 12.03.2022 at 5.30 p.m., while he was riding TVS XL, due to rash and negligent driving of rider of Bajaj Pulser bearing Reg.No.KA43W4809 and succumbed to injuries while taking treatment as contended in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?

ISSUE Nos.1 to 3 : These issues are inter connected.
Hence, they have taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition.

9. The case of the petitioners is that, one Krishnappa M., was died while giving treatment to the njuries sustained in a road traffic accident occurred on 12.03.2022 at about 4.30 p.m., on DandiganahalliVijayapura Raod, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru due to rash or negligent riding of Bajaj Pulsar Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA43W4809 by its rider.
Further case of the petitioners is that, the deceased was doing agriculture and earning more than Rs.25,000/ per month and contributed his entire earnings to the maintenance of the family.
The Vijayapura police have also registered the case against the rider of offending vehicle.
10. In order to prove the claim of petitioners, the 3 rd petitioner was examined as P.W.1 by filing affidavit.
P.W.1 also produced as many as 12 documents, which have been marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.

11. According to the respondent No.2, the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident, the petitioners have filed false case against the rider of offending vehicle.

Further the specific defence of the 2 nd respondent is that, after through investigation the police have filed charge sheet against the deceased by stating that, the deceased himself was solely responsible for the accident.
Further contended that, the rider of offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident.
2nd respondent also disputed the age and income of the deceased.
Deceased was not wearing helmet.
Hence, he contributed the negligence for the accident.

12. The 2nd respondent has examined its Assistant ManagerLegal namely Vishal Kumar V.
Paradeshi as R.W.1.
R.W.1 in his evidence affidavit has reiterated the written statement averments of 2nd respondent.

R.W.1 has produced his authorization letter as Ex.R.1 and true copy of Insurance Policy as Ex.R.2.
13.
Before going to discuss the issues, it is appropriate to say the admitted facts of the case.
There is no dispute with regard to death of Krishnappa M., in the road traffic accident.

The respondent No.2 has not seriously disputed the relationship of petitioners with deceased Krishnappa M.
14.

So, now the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent riding of offending vehicle or not and there is a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
In order to answer this aspect, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the rider of the offending vehicle as well as deceased.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle as well as deceased as per Ex.P.8.

It is relevant to note that, though the respondent No.2 has contended that, the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident,
however, in order to substantiate the same, the 2 nd respondent has not placed any material before this Tribunal.
Likewise, the petitioners have not challenged the charge sheet filed against the deceased.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and there is a contributory negligence from the side of deceased.

As such, this Tribunal determines the contributory negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and deceased in the ratio of 50:50.
15.
Now, the next aspect is with regard to age and income of the deceased.
In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 74 years.
P.W.1 was also deposed that, his father was aged about 74 years at the time of his death.
In order to substantiate the same, he has produced the Chikkanarayanamma vs Shivakumar .A

on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86514568/
5 notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased Krishnappa M., which is marked as Ex.P.9.
On careful perusal of this document, it reveals that, the year of birth of deceased Krishnappa M., is 1948.
The accident was occurred on 12.03.2022.
Therefore, age of the deceased is considered as 74 years at the time of accident.
16. Now, the next aspect is with respect to income of deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased doing agriculture and he was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
However, to substantiate the exact income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MVI) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/ per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
17. In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.

As such in the absence of authentic document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/ per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 12.03.2022.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,500/ per month.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 and 2 are answered in the Partly Affirmative, Issue No.3 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.4:
This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the son of deceased.
The 1 st petitioner has lost her husband and 2 nd and 3rd petitioners have lost their loving father.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth, which can never be equated in terms of the money.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency".
Hence, Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.

19. Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioners have established the age of deceased i.e.,
as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 74 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Chikkanarayanamma vs Shivakumar .A on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86514568/
6 Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident,
the income with respect to the future prospect has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".
"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
20. Admittedly, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 74 years and therefore, no additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
So, monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.15,500/, which would meet the ends of justice.
21. The 1st petitioner is the wife and 2nd petitioner is the daughter and 3rd petitioner is the son of deceased.
Already this court has observed that, petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are the dependents of the deceased.
Therefore, by applying the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
The same comes to Rs.15,500 - 5,166/ = Rs.10,334/.
Then total income of the deceased per annum comes to Rs.1,24,008/ (Rs.10,334 x 12 = 1,24,008/).
22. The deceased was 74 years old at the time of death, the multiplier 5 is applied, which is appropriate to the age of deceased.

Then the loss of dependency is calculated as hereunder:
Rs.1,24,008/ X 5 = Rs.6,20,040/. Therefore, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.6,20,040/ under the head of loss of dependency.
23.

P.W.1 in his affidavit has stated that, after the accident, his father was shifted to Akash Hospital,
Devanahalli.

After the death of his father, dead body was shifted to Community Health Center,
Vijayapura, Devanahalli Taluk for Postmortem.
P.W.1 deposed that, after postmortem, dead body was shifted to their village in a hired vehicle and performed last rites by spending Rs.1,00,000/ In order to substantiate his contention
, P.W.1 has not produced any documents.

24. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

sentences.text: The petitioners have contended that, they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
In order to substantiate the same, they have not produced any documents.
Now the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners No.2 and 3 are also entitled for consortium or not?

Admittedly, the 1st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled Chikkanarayanamma vs Shivakumar .A on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86514568/
7 for spousal consortium.
Admittedly the petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the son of deceased.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.

It is relevant to note that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others Case, observed that, the conventional heads namely filial consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses has to be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.

sentences.text: Therefore, the 1st petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/ under the head of spousal consortium and petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.44,000/ each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/ is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/ is awarded towards loss of estate.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.7,85,040/.
As discussed above, in so for as the contributory negligence factor is concerned, 50% of the contributory negligence is attributed to the deceased.

The adjudged compensation of Rs.7,85,040/ with interest at 6% p.a. is ordered to be proportionately paid by Insurance Company in the ratio of 50% and 50%
to be attributed to the deceased.
The insurance company shall pay Rs.3,92,520/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
26. Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, the rider of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to ride the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:
Respondent No.2 the insurance company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle.
Hence, it is held that, insurance coverage of the vehicle was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners.

The rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA43W4809 was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and it is clear violation of policy conditions.
The 2nd respondent has denied the age,
occupation and income of deceased, dependency of the petitioners on the deceased.

Further contended that, the rider of offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident.

however, in order to substantiate the same, the 2 nd respondent has not placed any material before this Tribunal.
Likewise, the petitioners have not challenged the charge sheet filed against the deceased.
Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and there is a contributory negligence from the side of deceased.
As such, this Tribunal determines the contributory negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and deceased in the ratio of 50:50.

As such in the absence of authentic document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/ per month.

So, monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.15,500/, which would meet the ends of justice.
